headline: Union Minister of Communications Shri Jyotiraditya Scindia Calls For Inclusive and Trusted Intelligent Finance at the Global Fintech Festival 2026
fullText:
Ministry of Communications

Union Minister of Communications Shri Jyotiraditya Scindia Calls For Inclusive and Trusted Intelligent Finance at the Global Fintech Festival 2026

Union Minister of Communications Hails India As The Data Capital Of The World

Broadband access grew from 6 crore to 103 crore in a decade, a 16x jump: Shri Scindia

Rolled out in 2022, India's 5G now covers 99.9% districts and 85% population in 26 months, with capex of Rs 4.5 lakh crore: Union Minister Shri Jyotiraditya Scindia

Smartphones are the new ‘bank branch’ for Indians: Union Minister of Communications

10 SEP 2026 10:30PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Communications and Development of North Eastern Region, Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia, called for an inclusive and trusted digital financial ecosystem, emphasising that before finance becomes intelligent, it must become inclusive. Speaking at the Global Fintech Festival 2026 in Mumbai, he said the telecom network, an invisible highway that cannot be seen, is the very foundation on which fintech evolves. Together with compute and trust, connectivity forms the new digital trinity powering the next phase of digital finance.

Highlighting the scale of India’s digital transformation, Shri Scindia said that around 25 crore people had access to the internet a decade ago, compared to 100 crore today. Broadband access has grown from just 6 crore to 103 crore, representing nearly 16 times growth in 10 years. He emphasised that technology must become ubiquitous, across India and the world.

The Union Minister said that smartphones have become bank branches, taking citizens from internet connectivity to credit and investment. With around 6.5 lakh villages becoming participants in the digital economy, he said every connected village can become a member of the global fintech ecosystem.

Highlighting India’s rapid 5G expansion, Shri Scindia said that following the launch of 5G in 2022, India achieved capability across 99.9% of districts, covering almost 85% of the population, within 26 months. Shri Scindia also noted that the rollout has been supported by over 5 lakh 5G base stations.

Furthermore, the Union Minister highlighted the sharp reduction in the cost of communications, noting that data costs have fallen to around 10 cents per GB. He said India has become the world’s cheapest data capital, making digital technology increasingly accessible.

Shri Scindia highlighted the journey of UPI, which began with around 90,000 transactions in its first month and has today scaled to more than 740 banks. UPI has processed around 24,162 crore transactions in FY 2025–26, worth approximately ₹314 lakh crore, demonstrating the scale that India’s Digital Public Infrastructure can achieve.

The Union Minister of Communications noted that 84% of domestic digital transactions take place on UPI, while India accounts for approximately 49% of the world’s real-time digital payment volumes. He credited the fintech ecosystem for this achievement and said that India’s success demonstrates the power of technology built at scale.

Union Minister Shri Scindia highlighted the success of UPI as an expression of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam. He said the technology is being taken to nine countries at no cost to them, while the world is looking towards taking this model to the next 20 countries.

Additionally, Shri Jyotiraditya Scindia said the architecture of digital finance rests on networks that carry connections, trust and interoperable platforms that connect institutions. He underlined three principles: innovation scales when infrastructure is open; inclusion scales when infrastructure is affordable; and trust scales when infrastructure is secure.

Highlighting the role of Jan Dhan accounts and DigiLocker, the Union Minister said around 60 crore Jan Dhan accounts and 9 billion documents on DigiLocker have dramatically reduced the distance between citizens and their ability to access finance. He emphasised that finance no longer needs to depend on the physical presence of a bank branch. “The smartphone is the bank branch,” he said, noting that a smartphone can take fintech to every citizen.

Shri Jyotiraditya Scindia highlighted that fintech connectivity has reached almost every village in the North Eastern Region, driven by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s impetus and sankalp. Through Digital Bharat Nidhi, around 22,000 towers are being established across 34,000 villages without telecom connectivity, with the objective of ensuring 100% saturation.

Shri Scindia said that as India works towards 100% saturation on the mobile front, a new arterial system is being established, extending from mobile to terrestrial networks. He highlighted the role of Gram Panchayats in creating first-mile, middle-mile and last-mile connectivity to reach the remaining villages.

The Union Minister also highlighted the national AI capabilities and compute power converge with digital infrastructure, AI can personalise financial advice and credit and increasingly make financial services autonomous.

Shri Scindia emphasised that with greater intelligence comes greater responsibility. He called for financial systems to be ring-fenced, with strong firewalls and safeguards to protect citizens and their financial security.

Sanchar Saathi, a Government of India initiative that protects citizens against suspicious connections and enables stolen devices to be blocked. Shri Scindia highlighted the AI powered tool- ASTR, which has helped disconnect more than 88 lakh suspicious mobile connections.

The Financial Fraud Risk Indicator ring-fences suspicious transactions and helps stop fraudulent payments before money leaves citizens’ accounts. He called for SOPs across banking networks to strengthen the protection of citizens and their financial capabilities.

Shri Jyotiraditya Scindia emphasised the need to shift from detecting fraud after it happens to preventing it before it occurs. He said the objective must be to move from reactive security to predictive trust.

The Union Minister called for the creation of a Trust Grid for finance, bringing together telecom, digital identity, UPI and financial systems. He said greater convergence of Aadhaar and UPI can give every citizen the capability to participate in and benefit from the digital economy.

Shri Scindia said that if Digital India democratised access, Intelligent India must democratise intelligence. AI cannot remain the preserve of corporates or banks. It must become a tool available to every citizen, enabling each person to benefit from the transformation underway.

The Union Minister highlighted India’s indigenous 4G telecom stack, noting that telecom stacks have historically been developed by a small number of countries and companies. India has now produced its own domestic 4G stack and is working on 5G.

Shri Scindia said India’s 6G mission has already started, with the ambition of contributing 10% of global 6G patents and becoming a valuable partner in the development of 6G standards.

Concluding, Shri Jyotiraditya Scindia said India must “Innovate in India, serve in India, serve the world and serve it securely.” He said the ambition must be to move from a connected India to intelligent digital finance and then to empowered finance, and from Digital Public Infrastructure to trusted infrastructure.

headline: Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan Launches Operational Guidelines for DILRMP 3.0
fullText:
Ministry of Rural Development

Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan Launches Operational Guidelines for DILRMP 3.0

Central Sector Scheme approved with an outlay of ₹565.50 Crore for 2026–2031 to establish an integrated, GIS-based ‘Land Stack’

Sub-Registrar Offices to be upgraded into modern ‘Registration Seva Kendras’ modeled after Passport Seva Kendras

Every land parcel to receive a 14-digit Bhu-Aadhaar (ULPIN) alongside full georeferencing of cadastral maps

“Land is not merely property; it represents the pride of farmers and our generational heritage”: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan

10 SEP 2026 10:01PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Rural Development, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan, formally launched the Operational Guidelines for the Digital India Land Records Modernisation Programme (DILRMP) 3.0 during a hybrid event held at Krishi Bhawan today. The launch brought together State Revenue and Registration Ministers, Principal Secretaries, and senior officials from across the country via video conferencing.

Addressing the gathering, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan stated that DILRMP 3.0 is a decisive step toward improving Ease of Living for rural citizens, farmers, and property owners. He underscored that land in India is deeply tied to emotional and familial identities, making accurate and accessible documentation vital.

“Land is not just a piece of soil; it is the pride of our farmers, the blessing of our ancestors, and the identity of future generations,” said the Union Minister.

The Minister pointed out that the earlier phases of DILRMP successfully digitized 99.90% of Records of Rights (RoRs) and 97% of cadastral maps, alongside computerizing 99% of Sub-Registrar Offices (SROs). He noted that DILRMP 3.0 now raises the bar by moving from isolated digitization to full system integration, ensuring farmers can secure institutional credit easily and citizens are spared repeated visits to government offices.

Speaking on the occasion, Minister of State for Rural Development, Dr. Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani, highlighted that DILRMP 3.0 will resolve legacy challenges by focusing on spatial accuracy, georeferenced maps, and seamless interoperability across departments.

Secretary, Department of Land Resources (DoLR), Shri Narendra Bhooshan, delivered the welcome address and set the context for the guidelines, noting that DILRMP 3.0 marks a shift toward building an integrated Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) for land administration. Joint Secretary (LR), Shri Parikipandla Narahari, gave a comprehensive presentation detailing the technical architecture and scheme components.

Key Highlights of DILRMP 3.0

GIS-enabled ‘Land Stack’: Land Stack, an integrated digital framework would bring together different layers of land-related information such as georeferenced cadastral maps, Records of Rights, property registrations, and relevant court matters through GIS based digital interfaces. It will enable different land-related systems to be connected and accessed in an interoperable manner, while allowing each State to develop its own Land Stack by integrating its various land-related datasets and systems through APIs. These State-level Land Stacks would, in turn, form the building blocks of a National Land Stack, which would be developed in a federated manner, enabling seamless interoperability and exchange of information across States while retaining the respective ownership and control of data with the concerned authorities.

Universal Bhu-Aadhaar (ULPIN): Assigns a 14-digit unique identifier to every land parcel in the country to establish unambiguous property identities and eliminate fraud.

Registration Seva Kendras (RSKs): High-footfall 75 Sub-Registrar Offices will be modernized into citizen-friendly service centers with digital queue management and improved amenities, drawing inspiration from Passport Seva Kendras.

Scanning of Legacy Records: Historical land and property registration records will be systematically scanned and digitally archived to protect inheritance rights and curb ancestral land disputes.

Registration Repository: A secure digital framework of registered deeds and encumbrance information to enable ownership verification, transaction history and property due diligence.

Paperless Revenue Courts: Modernizes the Revenue Court Case Management System (RCCMS) by linking it directly with land records to cut case pendency and expedite mutation settlements.

Urban Land Mapping (NAKSHA): Accelerates the NAKSHA pilot project to create accurate, GIS-based urban land records and issue Urban Property Cards (UrPro Cards).

Implementation and Monitoring

DILRMP 3.0 will be implemented across all States and Union Territories with 100% central funding under a phased, performance-linked mechanism managed through the Public Financial Management System (PFMS). Progress will be monitored in real time via an upgraded DILRMP-MIS dashboard overseen by the Project Sanctioning & Monitoring Committee (PS&MC). The event concluded with a vote of thanks proposed by the Director, DoLR.

headline: Union Minister Shri Manohar Lal to Participate in G20 Energy Abundance Ministerial Meeting in Houston, USA
fullText:
Ministry of Power

Union Minister Shri Manohar Lal to Participate in G20 Energy Abundance Ministerial Meeting in Houston, USA

11 SEP 2026 8:41AM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Power and Housing & Urban Affairs Shri Manohar Lal will participate in the G20 Energy Ministerial Meeting to be held in the Houston, United States of America from 14–16 September 2026. The meeting, hosted under the U.S. G20 Presidency, will bring together Energy Ministers and senior representatives from G20 members to deliberate on key issues concerning global energy security, affordability, infrastructure development and resilient energy supply chains.

The Minister will participate in ministerial sessions under three key pillars - “Energy Security and Affordable Baseload,” “Permitting and Regulatory Efficiency,” and “Critical Minerals & Resilient Supply Chains.” The discussions will focus on strengthening energy security and affordability, facilitating timely development of energy infrastructure through efficient regulatory frameworks, and building secure, resilient and diversified critical-mineral supply chains.

During the meeting, Shri Manohar Lal will seek to highlight India’s approach towards building a resilient and future-ready energy system capable of meeting its rapidly growing energy needs while sharing India’s experience in enhancing permitting and regulatory efficiency through institutional and policy reforms as well as highlighting India’s focus on diversification, circularity, and strengthening the entire value chain of critical minerals.

The Minister’s participation will reaffirm India’s commitment to constructive international engagement and collective action in addressing evolving global energy challenges. India will continue to advocate pragmatic, inclusive and technology-neutral approaches that respect diverse national circumstances and advance secure, affordable, reliable, resilient and sustainable energy systems for all.

headline: Critical Minerals Key to India’s Energy Security, Industrial Competitiveness and National Security: Union Minister Dr Jitendra Singh
fullText:
Ministry of Science & Technology

Critical Minerals Key to India’s Energy Security, Industrial Competitiveness and National Security: Union Minister Dr Jitendra Singh

Dr Jitendra Singh Says India Moves from Technology Follower to Confident Global Player; Calls for Stronger Industry-Research Partnerships and Domestic Capabilities

Dr Jitendra Singh Says India Must Combine Domestic Resources with Global Partnerships to Build Resilient Value Chains

Dr Jitendra Singh Calls for Whole-of-Nation Approach to Secure India’s Strategic Materials and Technology Future

Dr Jitendra Singh Pushes for Early Industry Linkages to Turn Research and Innovation into Commercial Success

11 SEP 2026 3:53PM by PIB Delhi

India is no longer a country that waits for others to experiment and then follows their success; it is now confident of shaping its own global role in emerging technologies, Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology, Earth Sciences, and MoS in the Prime Minister’s Office, Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh said today. Critical minerals are key to India’s Energy security, Industrial competitiveness and national security, he asserted.

The Minister said critical minerals and metals will be a driving component of the next phase of technological development, with their importance extending beyond mining to energy security, industrial competitiveness and national security.

Dr. Jitendra Singh was delivering the keynote address at the Special Plenary of the 3rd Global Summit on Advanced Materials, Critical Minerals, & Metals, organised by the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) at Silver Oak Hall, India Habitat Centre, New Delhi. The summit, themed “Building Resilient Value Chains for a Sustainable and Competitive Future,” brought together government, industry, research and international stakeholders.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said the global economy is undergoing a paradigm shift, with clean energy, electric mobility, semiconductors, telecommunications, aerospace, defence and nuclear energy emerging as major drivers of technological and industrial transformation. India, he said, is now participating in this global discourse with much greater confidence and is preparing to assume a larger global role.

He said the changing technological landscape makes it imperative for India to build capabilities across the entire value chain of critical minerals and advanced materials—from exploration and extraction to refining, processing, engineering and manufacturing. Domestic resources will have to be combined optimally with international resources, while indigenous technologies and globally competitive benchmarks are developed simultaneously.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said advanced materials and critical minerals require a whole-of-government and whole-of-nation approach, with industry being an integral partner. India has to pursue global strategies and international partnerships while strengthening its domestic technological capabilities, he said.

Referring to the government’s approach towards strategic sectors, the Minister said India has taken significant steps to bring private industry into areas that were traditionally considered beyond its reach. He referred particularly to the opening up of the nuclear sector to private players, describing it as an important change in India’s approach to strategic technology and investment.

He invited international investors and industry, including from Canada and other countries, to participate in the opportunities emerging from India’s opening up of the nuclear sector. He said the new framework provides room for foreign collaboration and investment along with greater domestic participation.

The Minister also referred to the RDI Fund, saying that the initiative announced by the Prime Minister has now moved into implementation. Such initiatives, he said, can help accelerate private-sector participation in strategic areas where industry has traditionally been hesitant to invest.

Dr. Jitendra Singh called for early industry linkage with research and innovation, saying potential industry partners should be brought on board right from the beginning. This would enable research initiatives to remain aligned with market requirements and improve their prospects of becoming commercially viable. He said a healthy synergy among research, industry, government and the non-government sector is essential for sustaining startups and entrepreneurs.

He said India needs to invest heavily in research and innovation and develop a stronger culture of financial support for knowledge creation. Philanthropy for research is an area where India can do much more, he said, urging industry and leading business houses to recognise research as an important form of philanthropy that contributes to the larger welfare of humanity.

Dr. Jitendra Singh also referred to India’s experience of using steel slag for road construction as an example of how collaboration between government and industry can turn what was earlier regarded as waste into a productive resource. He said the experience reinforces the principle that there is virtually no waste when materials are approached through innovation and appropriate technology.

The Minister set out five broad priorities for India’s strategic technology and materials ecosystem: heavy investment in research and innovation; building domestic capabilities to strengthen energy security; deeper partnerships among stakeholders; global and recycling models; and a stronger culture of philanthropy for research.

He said building domestic capabilities is particularly important for energy security as the world moves towards cleaner and greener sources of energy. India must reduce vulnerabilities arising from external dependence while preparing its industries and technologies for the requirements of a changing global energy landscape.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said India is at an important stage in its technological journey, with opportunities emerging across advanced materials, critical minerals, nuclear energy, space and other strategic sectors. “We are now much, much more confident” about India’s ability to assume a global role, he said, adding that the best is yet to come.

Calling for partnerships built with the highest degree of integrity, Dr. Jitendra Singh said India’s next phase of growth in strategic technologies and materials will depend on government, industry, researchers, startups, investors and international partners working together as equal stakeholders in the country’s technological journey.

headline: India’s Coastline Must be Viewed as an Integrated Space of Ecology, Security, Economy, Technology and Human Development: Dr. Jitendra Singh
fullText:
Ministry of Earth Sciences

India’s Coastline Must be Viewed as an Integrated Space of Ecology, Security, Economy, Technology and Human Development: Dr. Jitendra Singh

Coastal Ecology and Security Cannot be Addressed in Isolation; Need Holistic Coastal India Approach: Dr. Jitendra Singh

India’s 11,000–12,000 Km Long Coastline Offers Significant Potential for Marine Resources and 'Blue Economy'

Ocean Observation, Surveillance, Communication, Remote Sensing and Emerging Technologies Can Strengthen Coastal Security

Deep Ocean Mission and Indigenous Technologies Opening New Frontiers for Exploration of Marine Resources: Dr. Jitendra Singh

11 SEP 2026 3:49PM by PIB Delhi

India’s coastline must be viewed as an interconnected space of ecology, security, economy, technology and human development, Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology and Earth Sciences and MoS PMO, Personnel, Public Grievances, Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh, said today while virtually addressing the National Conference on Coastal Ecology, Security and Sustainability (CCESS) 2026. India’s 11,000–12,000 km long coastline offers significant potential for marine resources and the "Blue Economy", he added.

The Minister said that the country's long coastline and extensive marine ecosystem offer significant opportunities, while also requiring an integrated approach combining scientific knowledge, environmental sustainability, security and economic development.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said that India has an 11,000–12,000 km long coastal area, among the longest in the world, and emphasised the importance of the ocean and coastal regions in the country's future development. He said that India's historical association with the ocean also reflects the knowledge and understanding of the marine environment possessed by its ancestors.

Highlighting the importance of the Deep Ocean Mission, the Minister said that India is moving towards exploring the largely unexplored resources of the deep ocean while simultaneously building indigenous capabilities. He noted that a totally indigenous research vessel, ORV Sagar Manthan, was launched recently, reflecting efforts towards self-reliance in deep-ocean research and exploration.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said that robots and submersibles are being developed to explore the depths of the ocean. He also referred to the efforts to enhance India's capability for deep-sea exploration and said that the country's progress in this area would open up new possibilities for understanding and utilising marine resources.

The Minister linked deep-ocean exploration with India's emerging economic opportunities, saying that if the country is to take its economy to the next level, it will have to look towards resources that have not yet been fully explored. He identified marine and coastal resources, including metals, minerals and fisheries, as areas with significant potential.

Dr. Jitendra Singh highlighted the potential of marine resources to contribute to the country's economic development while ensuring environmental sustainability. Referring to research on black sulphite and minerals, he said that the possibility of extracting marine minerals in the future represents one of the areas being explored. He also highlighted work aimed at increasing the economic potential of fisheries.

The Minister emphasised that coastal communities are an integral part of the wider coastal ecosystem. He said that efforts to expand the economic potential of coastal resources must also focus on improving the livelihoods of communities living along the coast while ensuring protection of the environment.

Dr. Jitendra Singh highlighted the growing technological dimension of coastal security. He said that ocean observation, surveillance, communication, remote sensing, data and emerging technologies can play an important role in strengthening India's understanding of and preparedness for the coastal and marine environment.

The Minister said that these technological capabilities need to be brought together through a holistic Coastal India approach, with the combined participation of the Government and the wider nation. He emphasised that the challenges and opportunities associated with the coastline cannot be addressed by individual sectors working in isolation.

In this context, Dr. Jitendra Singh said that the National Conference on Coastal Ecology, Security and Sustainability (CCESS) 2026 provides an important platform for bringing together different areas of expertise. The conference's multidisciplinary character, involving earth sciences, academia, defence, maritime institutions, legal experts, industry and coastal stakeholders, provides an opportunity to develop an integrated understanding of coastal challenges.

The Minister emphasised that coastal ecology and coastal security cannot be addressed in isolation. He said that resilient coastal regions require healthy marine ecosystems, informed communities, effective governance and strong scientific capabilities.

Dr. Jitendra Singh highlighted the importance of connecting ocean science with national policy, so that scientific knowledge can contribute directly to coastal planning and management. He also emphasised the role of coastal communities, noting that their livelihoods, traditional knowledge and participation are integral to sustainable coastal development.

He said that India's coastal infrastructure and ports are central to connectivity, trade and economic growth, and that sustainable development of these assets requires a sound scientific understanding of coastal and marine environments.

Dr. Jitendra Singh also highlighted the "Swachh Sagar Surakshit Sagar" campaign, which has been undertaken for the past five years. He recalled that a 75-day campaign was launched in 2022 and involved participation from citizens and different stakeholders across coastal States.

The Minister said that the campaign would continue this year from 12 September to 19 September, with a range of activities including clean-up drives and participation of NGOs and organisations. He also highlighted the introduction of a pledge for keeping India's coastline clean, adding a citizen-participation component to the campaign.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said that the larger objective should be to develop a holistic Coastal Bharat approach in which environmental sustainability, economic opportunity, scientific capability and coastal security reinforce one another. fullText:
Ministry of Finance

Bankers’ Books Evidence Act, 2026 to come into force from 1st October 2026

The Act modernises the legal framework for use of banking records as evidence

Simplified and standardised certification to facilitate use of banking records in legal proceedings

11 SEP 2026 2:53PM by PIB Delhi

The Government has consistently pursued reforms to strengthen the banking and financial sector, promote ease of doing business and modernise the legal and regulatory framework in line with the evolving needs of the economy. With banking practices and technology evolving rapidly, laws governing banking records also need to keep pace with these changes.

The Bankers’ Books Evidence Act, 2026, which received the assent of the President on 13th August 2026, replaces the Bankers’ Books Evidence Act, 1891 and provides for a modern framework for the use of banking records as evidence in line with contemporary banking practices.

The notification dated 10th September 2026 (Gazette Notification link attached below) appoints 1st October 2026 as the date on which the provisions of the Act will come into force.

The Act adopts a technology-neutral approach by recognising banking records maintained in physical, electronic, digital, virtual, cloud-based and other contemporary forms. It also provides for simplified and standardised certification of banking records, including through manual, digital or electronic signatures.

Greater clarity has also been provided on the summoning of bank officials where the bank is not a party to the proceedings, with a “special cause” to be recorded in writing by the Court for such summoning.

Further, the Central Government may extend the provisions to specified financial sector entities or classes of entities, allowing the framework to cater to the evolving financial landscape.

These reforms reflect the Government’s continued commitment to modernising laws in line with technological advancements and evolving economic needs, promoting ease of doing business and strengthening a modern and efficient financial system.

headline: India Administers 80 Lakh HPV Vaccine Doses, Marking Major Milestone in Cervical Cancer Prevention
fullText:
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

India Administers 80 Lakh HPV Vaccine Doses, Marking Major Milestone in Cervical Cancer Prevention

More than 8 Million HPV Vaccine Doses Administered Under National HPV Vaccination Campaign

Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh and Mizoram Achieve 100% Coverage; Bihar, Andhra Pradesh and Assam Cross 90%

Uttar Pradesh Leads with More than 22 Lakh Adolescent Girls Vaccinated

All Vaccination Sessions Conducted Under Medical Supervision with 24×7 Arrangements for Management of Rare AEFI

National HPV Vaccination Campaign Launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in February 2026 to Provide Free, Voluntary Single-Dose Vaccination to 14-Year-Old Girls

11 SEP 2026 2:12PM by PIB Delhi

India has crossed a significant milestone in its efforts to prevent cervical cancer, with more than 80 lakh (8 million) doses of Human Papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine administered under the National HPV Vaccination Campaign since its launch in February 2026. The milestone marks the expanding reach of HPV vaccination through the public health system and reinforces India’s commitment to strengthening preventive healthcare for adolescent girls.

The National HPV Vaccination Campaign was launched by Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi in February 2026. Under the campaign, 14-year-old girls are provided voluntary and free-of-cost single-dose HPV vaccination, with parental consent, at Government health facilities.

As per Registrar General of India (RGI) 2021 estimates, approximately 1.2 crore girls constitute the annual cohort of 14-year-olds who are expected to benefit from the initiative each year.

States and Union Territories have made significant progress in expanding HPV vaccination coverage, with several States achieving complete coverage of their identified target cohorts.

Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh and Mizoram have achieved 100 per cent coverage of their respective identified target populations. Bihar, Andhra Pradesh and Assam have crossed 90 per cent coverage, while Karnataka has achieved more than 85 per cent coverage. Chhattisgarh, Sikkim, Kerala, Telangana and Odisha have crossed 60 per cent coverage.

Among States, Uttar Pradesh has recorded the highest number of vaccinations, with more than 22 lakh adolescent girls vaccinated under the campaign.

The progress reflects coordinated implementation by States and Union Territories, sustained community mobilisation and active engagement of district-level health teams. States have adopted context-specific approaches to reach eligible adolescent girls through the public health delivery network, including in rural, urban, remote and geographically challenging areas.

Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat have achieved 100 per cent coverage of their identified target cohorts, supported by sustained community mobilisation, coordinated implementation and focused field-level efforts. The progress in Assam and other Northeastern States also demonstrates the role of integrated community health networks and coordinated field-level action in expanding access across geographically diverse areas.

The campaign has placed strong emphasis on community engagement and credible information, with parents, healthcare providers, teachers and frontline health workers being actively engaged to address concerns and counter misinformation relating to HPV vaccination.

Healthcare providers, including paediatricians, gynaecologists and experts from institutions such as AIIMS, along with teachers and frontline health workers including ASHAs and ANMs, have supported awareness and mobilisation efforts across States and districts.

The campaign has also leveraged India’s digital health infrastructure through the U-WIN platform, enabling programme managers to monitor vaccination coverage at the district level, identify coverage gaps and missed beneficiaries, and support more effective programme planning and resource allocation.

The national campaign builds on extensive global experience with HPV vaccination. More than 800 million doses of HPV vaccines have been distributed globally, providing substantial real-world experience on their use and safety.

HPV vaccination, initially adopted predominantly by high-income countries, has progressively expanded into national immunisation programmes across countries at different income levels. At present, 87 per cent of upper-middle-income countries, 78 per cent of lower-middle-income countries and 54 per cent of low-income countries have adopted HPV vaccines in their National Immunization Programmes.

The growing adoption of HPV vaccination across diverse income settings reflects its increasing role as an important component of national strategies for cervical cancer prevention.

All vaccination sessions under the campaign are conducted under the supervision of trained Medical Officers at Government health facilities.

Government health facilities are also linked with 24×7 healthcare facilities for appropriate management of rare Adverse Events Following Immunization (AEFI). This mechanism ensures timely assessment, monitoring and management of any vaccination-related adverse event.

With the campaign progressing towards its final phase, the focus remains on reaching the remaining eligible beneficiaries and ensuring that no eligible girl is left behind.

The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare continues to work closely with States and Union Territories, healthcare professionals, frontline health workers and communities to strengthen awareness, facilitate access and support effective implementation of the HPV Vaccination Campaign.

The achievement of 80 lakh HPV vaccine doses marks an important step in India’s efforts to strengthen preventive healthcare and advance long-term protection against cervical cancer among future generations.

headline: Monsoon Resilience: Captive Mines Delivering Growth
fullText:
Ministry of Coal

Monsoon Resilience: Captive Mines Delivering Growth

11 SEP 2026 2:01PM by PIB Delhi

Captive mines have been a mainstay of coal production, and their output has grown steadily. Production from captive mines rose from 167.44 MT in FY 2024-25 to 184 MT in FY 2025-26, a growth of 10.10%. Along with commercial mines, which produced ~26 MT, the captive and commercial segment together accounted for 210 MT in FY 2025-26 against 190.95 MT the previous year. Captive and Commercial mines account for about 21% of total domestic coal production, which stood at 1,039 MT in FY 2025-26 and has remained above one billion tonnes for the second year running.

The performance has carried into the current year. Captive mines produced 68.98 MT up to 10 September 2026, against 65.78 MT in the corresponding period of FY 2025-26. This is a growth of about 5%, or an additional 3.2 MT, and it comes on a base that was itself 10.12% higher than the year before it. The gain has been recorded in the first five months of the year, which include the monsoon, when mining and evacuation are at their most difficult. Dispatch from captive mines has also been better than previous year. Captive mines dispatched 75.68 MT against 71.43 MT last year, a growth of 5.94% and an increase of 4.25 MT.

Provisional figures indicate the pace picking up further as the monsoon begins to recede. In the ten days between 01 September and 10 September 2026, captive mines produced 4.12 MT and dispatched 4.21 MT.

New capacity is being added steadily to this base. Nine captive & commercial mines are expected to commence production during FY 2026-27, with a combined peak rated capacity of 20.67 MT. Three of these, with peak capacity of 7.51 MT, have already started production during the current year. The remaining six, are expected to commence production soon during the year.

On this footing, production from captive mines is expected to cross 190 MT in FY 2026-27. Together with commercial mines, the two segments are expected to exceed 228 MT during the current financial year.

headline: Facts on Auction of Tara (Revised) Coal Block
fullText:
Ministry of Coal

Facts on Auction of Tara (Revised) Coal Block

11 SEP 2026 12:40PM by PIB Delhi

Recently, reports have appeared in media on the auction of the Tara Coal block. These reports are misleading and incomplete facts have been used in these reports. These reports do not take into account the important developments that took place after 2023, which ultimately led to the auction of Tara (Revised) Coal Block in 2026.

It is a fact that the Tara coal block offered under the 7th Tranche in 2023 was taken out of commercial coal mine auctions as letter was received from Government of Chhattisgarh for the exclusion of coal blocks in Hasdeo Arand area from the commercial coal mine auctions.

Accordingly, the coal blocks in Hasdeo Arand area having overlap with Lemru elephant corridor were not offered in the subsequent tranches of commercial coal mine auctions.

However, a letter dated 11.12.2025 was received from Government of Chhattisgarh to include the Tara coal block stating that “the coal block is outside the Lemru Elephant Corridor, and the coal block may be offered in the upcoming tranche of auction”.

Accordingly, the coal block was put up for auction under the 15th round of commercial coal mine auction duly removing the influence zone of Lemru Elephant Corridor and has been successfully auctioned.

It is pertinent to mention that the coal block has gathered a lot of interest from the market. A total of 9 bids were received for the coal block under the 15th round. The Block has been auctioned at a revenue share of 37.50%. The Coal Block is expected to generate annual revenue of more than Rs 1200 crores to the state and generate employment for more than 8000 people.

It is clear from above that Tara Coal Block was excluded from auction in July 2023 after considering the concerns raised by the Government of Chhattisgarh. It was considered for auction again only after the State Government’s communication dated 11.12.2025 and after revision of the block boundary by CMPDIL. Therefore, the reports do not present the complete facts and overlooks important developments that led to the auction of Tara (Revised) Coal Block.

headline: Commerce and Industry Minister Shri Piyush Goyal Calls for Deeper, Resilient and More Balanced Intra-BRICS Trade
fullText:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry

Commerce and Industry Minister Shri Piyush Goyal Calls for Deeper, Resilient and More Balanced Intra-BRICS Trade

Shri Goyal Urges Member Countries to Open Markets and Simplify Regulatory Procedures

Shri Goyal Urges BRICS Member And Partner Countries to Link Payment Systems And Promote Trade in Each Other’s Local Currencies

Shri Goyal Emphasises Greater Cooperation in Agriculture, Pharmaceuticals, Engineering, Electronics, Automobiles, Services, Startups and Emerging Technologies

Union Minister of External Affairs Dr. S. Jaishankar Highlights Supply Chain Connectivity, Trade Facilitation and Innovation as Key BRICS Priorities

11 SEP 2026 12:10PM by PIB Delhi

With BRICS accounting for nearly one-fourth of global trade, Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal today underlined the need for member and partner countries to build deeper, more resilient and balanced trade partnerships. Addressing the Opening Session of the BRICS Business Forum in New Delhi, Shri Goyal emphasised greater market access, diversified supply chains and simpler regulatory procedures to unlock the full potential of economic cooperation. He expressed hope that the Forum would deliver significant outcomes and take economic dialogue and business partnerships among BRICS countries to the next level.

The Opening Session was also addressed by H.E. Maxim Reshetnikov, Minister of Economic Development of the Russian Federation; Union Minister of External Affairs Dr. S. Jaishankar; Minister of State for Ministry of Commerce & Industry and Ministry of Electronics & Information Technology Shri Jitin Prasada; and Commerce Secretary Shri Rajesh Agrawal.

Shri Goyal said India is an important pillar of intra-BRICS trade and highlighted the country’s strong capabilities in engineering goods and electronics, which account for the largest segment of India’s manufactured exports. He also noted that India is known as the pharmacy of the world. He said India sees BRICS as an important market for these and other products that it seeks to take to the world as a trusted partner.

Emphasising the importance of deep and resilient trade among partners, Shri Goyal said supply chains must be diversified and trade should not become an impediment to growth and the well-being of people in any member state. He called upon BRICS countries to open their markets for each other’s products, including raw materials and critical minerals.

Shri Goyal said supply chains would be resilient when they run both ways. Noting that non-tariff measures impose higher export costs than tariffs themselves for 88 per cent of countries, he called for easier and smoother market access. He urged BRICS member and partner countries to open their markets while working together to simplify regulatory procedures and facilitate faster clearance of consignments.

Calling for greater cooperation in agriculture, Shri Goyal urged BRICS countries to encourage agri-tech startups to jointly develop solutions for farmers across BRICS nations in the interest of food security. He also called upon countries to open their services markets to each other in a real sense, facilitate the movement of professionals across borders and make it easier to recognise each other’s professional qualifications.

Highlighting women’s participation in India’s startup and entrepreneurship ecosystem, Shri Goyal said that more than 45 per cent of the 250,000 recognised startups in India have at least one woman partner or director. He said two-thirds of the small loans provided in the last decade have been given to women entrepreneurs, helping them stand on their own feet and become independent and self-reliant. Referring to the meeting of the BRICS Women’s Business Alliance in New Delhi earlier in the week, he said he had urged the Alliance to ensure that women-led enterprises participate in every BRICS exhibition, trade fair and other opportunities that could be encouraged and supported.

Shri Goyal highlighted India’s significant initiatives in laying out digital public infrastructure and said that the Unified Payments Interface (UPI) today has over 250 billion transactions a year, representing more than half of transactions by volume across the world. He said UPI is also accepted in 11 countries and urged BRICS member and partner countries to link their payment systems, promote trade in each other’s local currencies, make digital trade global and build together for emerging technologies.

He said India brings strong capabilities across sectors including agriculture, pharmaceuticals, engineering, electronics, automobiles and auto components and services, and called for linking startup ecosystems as well. He said these trends offer significant scope for joint innovation, technology partnerships and resilient global value chains.

As India moves towards Viksit Bharat 2047, the collective goal that 1.4 billion Indians have set for themselves to make India a developed nation when the country celebrates 100 years of independence, Shri Goyal said there is immense potential to deepen cooperation with BRICS members and partner countries. He expressed hope that the thematic sessions would lead to constructive and actionable recommendations to further strengthen intra-BRICS trade and economic cooperation.

Union Minister of External Affairs Dr. S. Jaishankar in his address said that this year marks 20 years of institutionalised BRICS cooperation, during which BRICS has evolved substantially in membership, agenda and mechanisms of cooperation. He said India’s Chairship has sought to carry this evolution forward through the theme of resilience, innovation, cooperation and sustainability. He said these priorities are especially relevant as the global political and economic order undergoes churn, with volatility, uncertainty and complexity becoming defining features, while geopolitical conflicts, pandemics, climate-related disruptions, digitisation and technological advances are reshaping the economic landscape.

Dr. Jaishankar said resilience has become a key component of the BRICS community, with the BRICS Business Council and BRICS Women’s Business Alliance playing an important role in bringing industry, entrepreneurs and business leaders into the BRICS process. He said supply chain connectivity and trade facilitation have emerged as crucial, alongside services, agriculture and agritechnology, digital delivery, MSMEs, startups and women-led enterprises. He stressed the need for greater self-reliance while remaining connected and competitive through genuine market practices, dependable logistics, a predictable business environment, diversified commercial relationships and transparent trade and investment. He also highlighted digital public infrastructure, artificial intelligence, fintech and advanced manufacturing as major opportunities, while noting questions of access, standards, security and trust.

Dr. Jaishankar said India’s Chairship has sought to strengthen the innovation and entrepreneurial ecosystem through the BRICS incubator network and BRICS Startup Innovation Fund, stressing that the benefits must be accessible across the full spectrum of business communities. He said India’s experience makes it a natural partner, with a large and growing market, expanding manufacturing capabilities, deeper pools of talent, digital experience and a dynamic innovation and entrepreneurial base. As BRICS leaders prepare to meet, he said the Forum’s most useful contribution would be to bring a clear business perspective to the next phase of BRICS cooperation, focusing on opportunities, challenges faced by businesses and what governments can do to address them.

Speaking at the Opening session Minister of State for Ministry of Commerce & Industry and Ministry of Electronics & Information Technology Shri Jitin Prasada highlighted that BRICS Business Forum provides an opportunity to convert the strength of BRICS economies into concrete commercial results. He highlighted digital services, particularly artificial intelligence, as an important area of collaboration, noting its potential to improve productivity, standard of living, incomes and outcomes for individuals and MSMEs, while ensuring access to compute, particularly in the Global South.

Shri Prasada stressed the need for greater technology exchange and cooperation in AI while keeping the United Nations at the centre of governance. On semiconductors, he highlighted India’s Semiconductor Mission 2.0 with a financial outlay of about USD 13 billion in incentives and called for collaboration to develop the entire semiconductor ecosystem.

He also highlighted Digital Public Infrastructure and data centres as areas of cooperation, including sharing India’s best practices, and called for BRICS countries to co-develop, co-invest and co-innovate, with greater resources for research and development and startups to enable young people to access markets across international borders.

Commerce Secretary Shri Rajesh Agrawal said that BRICS represents a significant and growing market, with trade among BRICS countries rising from USD 84 billion in 2003 to nearly USD 1.2 trillion in 2024.

He emphasised preserving and revitalising the multilateral trading system with the WTO at its core and supporting MSMEs through affordable working capital, with the Jaipur Consensus providing a foundation for exploring a common BRICS mechanism.

Shri Agrawal highlighted strengthening global value chains through BRICS Connect, B2B partnerships, an annual BRICS Trade and Investment Expo, digital trade documentation and greater sectoral cooperation, including healthcare. He called for stronger economic integration just under the BRICS Economic Partnership Strategy 2030 through cooperation, trust, innovation and shared prosperity. Concluding his statement, Shri Agrawal wished the BRICS Business Forum every success.

headline: From Hospitals to Police, From CWCs to Grassroots Workers: Delhi Workshop Unites Stakeholders against Illegal Adoption
fullText:

From Hospitals to Police, From CWCs to Grassroots Workers: Delhi Workshop Unites Stakeholders against Illegal Adoption

Workshop organised with the theme “ Legal Adoption.Safe Childhood.Secure Future.Say No to Illegal Adoption”

11 SEP 2026 10:16AM by PIB Delhi

The Central Adoption Resource Authority (CARA), under the aegis of the Ministry of Women and Child Development, Government of India, in collaboration with the Department of Women and Child Development, Government of NCT of Delhi, and the Delhi State Adoption Resource Agency (SARA), organised an Adoption Awareness Workshop at the Main Auditorium, Delhi Secretariat, New Delhi, under the theme: “Legal Adoption. Safe Childhood. Secure Future. Say No to Illegal Adoption.

The workshop was graced by the presence of Smt. Bhavna Saxena, CEO, CARA; Smt. Rashmi Singh, Secretary, Department of Women and Child Development, Government of NCT of Delhi; Smt. Neha Yadav, DCP, SPUWAC; Smt. Monica Bharadwaj, Additional CP, Crime, Delhi Police; Shri O.P. Vyas, Chairperson, DCPCR, Dr. Anil Yadav, CMO, Outer North District; and other senior officials and stakeholders from the child protection, adoption ecosystem, Health & Police Departments.

The workshop brought together around 200 participants involved in child protection and adoption to strengthen awareness about the legal, transparent and child-centric adoption process and to create greater awareness about the risks and serious consequences of illegal adoption practices.

Speaking on the occasion, Smt. Bhavna Saxena, CEO, CARA, emphasised that awareness and vigilance across the entire child protection ecosystem are essential to safeguarding children from illegal adoption practices. “Every child deserves a safe childhood, a secure future and the protection of the law. There can be no shortcuts when it comes to adoption. Through this year’s campaign, CARA seeks to ensure that every stakeholder understands their role in preventing illegal adoption and that every prospective adoptive parent follows the legal adoption process. Together, we must ensure that the best interests, rights and dignity of every child remain at the heart of adoption.”

Speaking at the workshop, Smt. Rashmi Singh, Secretary, Department of Women and Child Development, Government of NCT of Delhi, said that the participation of stakeholders across the child protection ecosystem—from the Health and Police Departments, ANMs and Anganwadi workers to District Child Protection Units and Child Welfare Committees—marked a significant step towards wider sensitisation. She emphasised that such collective efforts reflect a strong institutional commitment to ensuring safe and secure childhoods.

As part of the awareness initiative, a fiction film on legal adoption was launched during the workshop. The film seeks to communicate the importance of following the authorised adoption process and highlight the risks associated with illegal adoption in an accessible and impactful manner.

Three Thematic Sessions Address Emerging Challenges

The workshop featured three focused technical sessions covering critical aspects of prevention and response to illegal adoption: Session 1 “Illegal Adoption: Emerging Trends, Challenges and State/National Response”, Session 2 “Role of Hospitals/Nursing Homes, Health Systems, Police & Judiciary in Preventing Illegal Adoption” and Session 3 “Strengthening Child Protection System: SARAs, CWCs, DCPUs, CCIs”

The sessions focused not only on strengthening coordination among State Adoption Resource Agencies (SARAs), Child Welfare Committees (CWCs), District Child Protection Units (DCPUs), and Child Care Institutions (CCIs), but also on sensitising key stakeholders from the Police, Health, and Anganwadi sectors to ensure the effective implementation of child protection and legal adoption mechanisms.

Real-Life Experience Sharing: From Challenge to Action

A special experience-sharing session was also organised during the workshop, featuring the real-life experience of Shri Arun Sharma, DCPO, on combating illegal adoption. The session provided participants with practical insights into the challenges faced on the ground, the importance of timely intervention and the role of field-level child protection functionaries in responding to suspected cases of illegal adoption.

Interactive Quiz Concludes the Workshop

The workshop concluded with an interactive quiz session designed to assess participants’ understanding and retention of key information shared during the various sessions. The engaging format encouraged participants to reflect on the legal provisions, roles and responsibilities discussed during the workshop and helped reinforce key messages relating to legal adoption, child protection and prevention of illegal adoption.

A play presented by DMRC Salam Baalak Trust sensitised participants on child rights, child protection & Safety, highlighting the collective responsibility to ensure a safe, secure and supportive environment for every child.

Focus on Combating Illegal Adoption

The theme for National Adoption Awareness Month–2026, has been selected as “Legal Adoption. Safe Childhood. Secure Future. Say No to Illegal Adoption!”. It is to emphasise that, Illegal adoption not only violates the provisions of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015, but can also deprive children of their legal safeguards, rights and protection. Such practices undermine the transparent, regulated and child-centric adoption system established under law.

The awareness initiative brought focus on the role of Women and Child Development Departments, Child Welfare Committees (CWCs), District Child Protection Units (DCPUs), Specialised Adoption Agencies (SAAs), Child Care Institutions, Health and Police Departments, Judiciary, Legal Services Authorities, hospital administrators, medical professionals, ASHA and ANM workers, civil society organisations and media representatives, among other stakeholders.

Participants were sensitised about the importance of coordinated action, timely intervention and adherence to the legal adoption framework to protect the rights and best interests of children.

“Legal Adoption. Safe Childhood. Secure Future. Say No to Illegal Adoption!” is not merely a campaign message, but a collective call to action to ensure that every child’s right to safety, dignity, identity and a secure family environment is protected.

headline: Seventh Gender Samvaad emphasises strengthening women’s leadership and agency in livelihoods
fullText:
Ministry of Rural Development

Seventh Gender Samvaad emphasises strengthening women’s leadership and agency in livelihoods

11 SEP 2026 9:52AM by PIB Delhi

The Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana– National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM), Ministry of Rural Development, in collaboration with the Institute for What Works to Advance Gender Equality (IWWAGE), organized the seventh edition of Gender Samvaad on the theme “Participation to Leadership: Enhancing Women’s Agency in Livelihoods.”

The dialogue witnessed participation from over 6 lakh stakeholders across the country, including SHG women, State Rural Livelihoods Mission staff, policymakers, gender experts, and practitioners, providing a platform for exchange of experiences and to deliberate on strengthening women’s participation, leadership and decision-making in rural livelihoods and economic institutions.

In his keynote address, Secretary, Ministry of Rural Development, Shri Rohit Kansal highlighted the Gender Samvaad’s journey from 1,400 participants in April 2021 to nearly six lakh in September 2025, reflecting the growing voice and leadership. He emphasised the strength of the SHG movement with over 10 crore women being exemplary across the world as a women-led movement. Highlighting state-led innovations, he shared about Maharashtra’s Women Farmers’ Empowerment Bill recognising women farmers without formal land titles, Odisha’s Bhubaneswar Declaration advancing women’s land rights and representation in agricultural institutions, and Andhra Pradesh’s RySS natural farming model, driven at scale by women’s SHGs.

He also highlighted that over 3.46 crore Lakhpati Didis earning more than ₹1 lakh annually is equally strengthening women’s economic aspirations. He underscored the need to identify, adapt and scale such innovations across States and strengthen women’s role as producers, entrepreneurs, decision-makers and leaders in building a Viksit Bharat.

Welcoming the participants, Joint Secretary-RL, Ministry of Rural Development, Shri Amit Shukla highlighted the evolution of gender integration under DAY-NRLM- from mobilisation to institutionalising gender as a mainstream concern in programme design and implementation. He noted that initiatives such as the Gender Advisory issued in December 2021, Nayi Chetna as the Annual National Gender Campaign, the Gender Integration Workshop, and the Practice Guide for Gender Integration in Livelihoods have progressively strengthened this approach. Emphasising the next frontier of women’s collective economic institutions, including CLFs, Producer Groups, Producer Enterprises and FPOs, he called for stronger governance and managerial capacities, financial record-keeping and credit-readiness, particularly in the context of the UN International Year of Women Farmers 2026.

Smt. Swati Sharma, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Rural Development, highlighted the ongoing National Campaign on Entrepreneurship-II (21 August–21 November 2026) as an important step towards strengthening entrepreneurship among SHG women through enterprise development, value chains, digital platforms and market access. She emphasised that collectivisation through SHGs, federations, Producer Groups, FPOs/FPCs and Producer Enterprises, supported by financial inclusion, skills, technology, market linkages and asset ownership, is critical to strengthening women’s economic agency and leadership. She called for a whole-of-government and convergence approach, bringing together Ministries and Departments, technical and research institutions, academia, civil society and development partners to mainstream gender across livelihood and entrepreneurship initiatives.

Other speakers enriched the dialogue with diverse insights and approaches. Smt. Garima Sai Sundaram, SPM–Non-Farm Livelihoods, Madhya Pradesh, highlighted how economic empowerment and access to resources strengthen women’s bargaining power and sustain their leadership. Smt. Seema Kulkarni, MAKAAM, emphasised the need for social protection and support systems to enable women’s participation and leadership. Prof. Nitya Rao, Gender and Livelihoods Expert, underscored convergence, institutional support, addressing unpaid care work and gaps in resource ownership, and access to appropriate tools and technologies to strengthen women’s economic identity, representation and sustainable leadership.

Women leaders from Assam and Maharashtra shared their journeys from SHG membership to entrepreneurship, leadership and decision-making. Smt. Niharika Bhuyan from Sonitpur, Assam, progressed from an SHG member to a leader in a women-led FPC, highlighting how collective action, training and institutional support enabled women farmers to strengthen their economic participation and decision-making. Smt. Kirti Tai Deshmukh from Akola, Maharashtra, moved from being a homemaker to an entrepreneur, demonstrating how SHG-based training and access to government schemes helped her establish her enterprise, build confidence and inspire other women to pursue entrepreneurship.

The Seventh Gender Samvaad, aligned with the UN International Year of Women Farmers 2026, provided a national platform to recognise and amplify the contributions of women farmers and their livelihood institutions to rural livelihoods, food systems and local economies. Launched in April 2021 as a joint initiative of DAY-NRLM and IWWAGE, Gender Samvaad has evolved into a national platform for knowledge exchange and policy dialogue, reaffirming gender equality as a key driver of women’s economic empowerment and inclusive rural development.

headline: 50 Years of ICAR–ICRISAT Partnership Celebrated at Dryland Congress 2026
fullText:

50 Years of ICAR–ICRISAT Partnership Celebrated at Dryland Congress 2026

Experts Deliberate on Resilient Farming Systems, Seed Systems, Gender and Youth-Centred Transformation

11 SEP 2026 8:28PM by PIB Delhi

The second day of Dryland Congress 2026 in New Delhi today featured a special session commemorating 50 years of collaboration between the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) and the International Crops Research Institute for the Semi-Arid Tropics (ICRISAT). The session brought together former and current leaders of both institutions to reflect on five decades of partnership and deliberate on a roadmap for strengthening collaboration and accelerating agricultural transformation towards Viksit Bharat 2047.

The special session was co-chaired by Dr R. S. Paroda, Former Director General, ICAR, and Dr William D. Dar, Former Director General, ICRISAT. Former leaders of ICAR and ICRISAT, including Dr Panjab Singh, Former Secretary, DARE and Director General, ICAR; Dr C. L. L. Gowda, Former Deputy Director General, ICRISAT; Dr T. R. Sharma, Former Deputy Director General, Crop Science, ICAR; and Dr Swapan Datta, Former Deputy Director General, Crop Science, ICAR, shared their reflections on the evolution and achievements of the partnership.

Dr M. L. Jat, Secretary, Department of Agricultural Research and Education (DARE) and Director General, ICAR, provided a strategic outlook for the partnership and emphasised the need to leverage the complementary strengths of ICAR and ICRISAT to address emerging agricultural challenges and create greater impact. He said, “We value the partnership, we support the partnership, and we will continue to support the partnership. By leveraging the complementary strengths of ICAR and ICRISAT, we can take on bigger challenges and create greater impact in the years ahead.”

Looking ahead, Dr D. K. Yadava, Deputy Director General, Crop Science, ICAR, and Dr Raman Babu, Global Research Program Director, Accelerated Crop Improvement, ICRISAT, presented a roadmap for strengthening ICAR–ICRISAT collaboration towards Viksit Bharat 2047, with emphasis on leveraging scientific capabilities and translating research into greater impact.

The second day of the Congress also featured three thematic panel discussions on “Reimagining Resilient Dryland Farming Systems,” “Transforming Seed Systems in the Global South,” and “Gender and Youth-Centered Transformation.” The discussions examined integrated and climate-smart approaches for smallholder farmers, strengthening seed delivery systems and public-private partnerships across Asia and Africa, and promoting inclusive policies, leadership and youth engagement in dryland agri-food systems.

These deliberations were complemented by parallel technical sessions covering resilient dryland farming systems, seed systems in the Global South, and gender- and youth-centred transformation. The sessions brought together researchers, policymakers, development partners and other stakeholders to discuss approaches for strengthening resilience, improving access to agricultural innovations and ensuring greater participation of women and young people in dryland agriculture.

Poster presentations also commenced as part of the Congress, with students and research scholars showcasing their scientific research. More than 145 posters are being evaluated on 10 and 11 September for the Best Poster Awards, providing a platform for emerging researchers to present their work and engage with experts from India and abroad.

A key highlight of the day was a visionary talk by Dr R. S. Paroda, Former Secretary, DARE and Director General, ICAR, on “Agrobiodiversity for Building Resilience of Drylands.” He highlighted the importance of conserving and effectively utilising agrobiodiversity to strengthen the resilience and sustainability of dryland farming systems.

Speaking on the 50-year partnership, Dr Himanshu Pathak, Director General, ICRISAT, said that the collaboration between ICAR and ICRISAT had translated scientific research into impact and that the next phase should focus on strengthening innovation, South-South cooperation and collective action for accelerating the transformation of drylands in India and beyond.

Dr R. S. Paroda said that the 50-year milestone was an opportunity to celebrate the achievements of the partnership while also looking ahead, adding that aligning resources, expertise and vision could accelerate the transformation of dryland agriculture.

Dr Panjab Singh highlighted the significant outcomes achieved through the ICAR–ICRISAT partnership over the past five decades and stressed that the next phase should focus on scaling successful models and ensuring that innovations reach farmers on a larger scale.

Dr William D. Dar emphasised that the future of dryland agriculture would depend on combining scientific capabilities with strong partnerships, innovation and scale, with greater focus on income security, nutrition security and resilience of farming communities.

On gender and youth-centred transformation, Prof. Yaye Gassama, ICRISAT Board Member, emphasised the importance of greater participation of women and young people in shaping solutions for dryland regions through leadership, innovation and enterprise.

Dr A. V. Bhavani Shankar, Chief General Manager, NABARD, highlighted the importance of developing scalable innovations and taking them beyond individual interventions towards systems-level and landscape-level deployment. He noted that the discussions at the Congress had emphasised the need to strengthen the scaling of innovations for wider impact.

The second day of Dryland Congress 2026 focused on strengthening institutional partnerships, accelerating scientific innovation, building resilient farming and seed systems, and ensuring greater participation of women and youth in the transformation of dryland agri-food systems. The Congress will conclude with further deliberations on pathways for translating scientific knowledge and partnerships into scalable solutions for dryland regions.

headline: Sarbananda Sonowal chairs 2nd Governing Council meeting of National Maritime Heritage Complex Society, reviews progress at Lothal
fullText:
Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways

Sarbananda Sonowal chairs 2nd Governing Council meeting of National Maritime Heritage Complex Society, reviews progress at Lothal

Phase 1A crosses 82% physical progress; 13 nations sign MoUs for India's maritime heritage project

13 nations already on board, as global collaboration effort for NMHC Lothal expands towards 35+ countries

11 SEP 2026 8:08PM by PIB Delhi

The Union Minister of Ports, Shipping & Waterways, Sarbananda Sonowal, chaired the 2nd Governing Council Meeting of the National Maritime Heritage Complex (NMHC) Society, reviewing the progress of the ambitious project coming up at Lothal, Gujarat, that seeks to revive and showcase India's maritime legacy spanning over five millennia.

Calling NMHC one of the most significant cultural and maritime initiatives undertaken by the Government of India, Sonowal said the project aims to establish Lothal as a globally renowned centre of maritime heritage, knowledge, education and tourism. "NMHC at Lothal is one of the most significant cultural and maritime initiatives undertaken by the Government of India," Sonowal said, recalling that the Governing Council had laid down a clear vision and direction when it first met in June 2025.

The Union Minister noted that the Society has since completed key statutory registrations, including income tax exemption, CSR and Darpan registrations, strengthening its institutional framework for future resource mobilisation. He was particularly encouraged by the international response the project has received, with 13 countries, including Portugal, the UAE, Vietnam, Thailand, the Netherlands, Denmark, Oman, Israel, Germany, the Republic of Korea, Italy, New Zealand and Singapore, having signed MoUs for collaboration, with discussions underway with several more nations towards a proposed pipeline of 35-plus partnerships. "These partnerships are enabling exchange of artefacts, replicas, ship models, research collaboration and cultural engagement, making NMHC a powerful instrument of maritime diplomacy," Sonowal said.

On construction progress, the Council was informed that Phase 1A has reached approximately 82 percent physical completion. The Minister urged implementing agencies to maintain strict supervision to meet the revised completion target of 31 October 2026, flagging components such as Galleries 4 and 6, Lothal Town and Aquatic Theming that remain to be completed. He also drew attention to 1,492 artefacts already readied for installation, calling for expedited approvals so exhibits can be commissioned in time for visitor operations.

Looking beyond the museum, the Council reviewed plans for Phase 1B and Phase 2, which will add further galleries, a 5D Dome Theatre, Coastal States Pavilion, a Lighthouse Museum planned in collaboration with the Directorate General of Lighthouses and Lightships (DGLL), a Maritime Research Institute (MRI) being developed with the Indian Maritime University (IMU), a Museotel and an Eco Resort. The proposed Lighthouse Museum, the Minister noted, has the potential to become the world's tallest lighthouse museum.

The Governing Council also took note of progress on external infrastructure, including the completed Dholera Expressway, a finalised plan for the high-speed rail corridor, and ongoing excavation at Lothal, now at 70 percent, being carried out by the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI), alongside continued support from the Government of Gujarat on connectivity, power, water and visitor amenities. The Council additionally considered and approved the proposed NMHC Bye-laws, providing a governance framework for the Society's transition into a fully operational institution.

Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal attributed the momentum behind the project to the vision of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, under whose leadership India's maritime heritage has been placed at the centre of national policy. "Under the dynamic leadership of Prime Minister Modi, we are not just building a museum at Lothal, we are reviving five thousand years of India's maritime civilisation and presenting it to the world," Sonowal said.

Sonowal thanked the NMHC team, IPRCL, the Government of Gujarat, the Indian Navy, IMU, major ports and partner ministries for their contribution, expressing confidence that with continued momentum, NMHC would emerge as a global landmark celebrating India's maritime legacy and future aspirations. "With collective effort, coordinated action and continued guidance from this Governing Council, I am confident that the National Maritime Heritage Complex will emerge as a global landmark," he said.
